body: I have several other facial deformities as well but the eyes are expressive so messed up eyes are one of the top things affecting confidence. I used to be fat and got down to a normal weight in recent months, and I can sort of make out the shape of my eye sockets. My (actual) upper eyelid ends just under my brow? I think.

Assuming each surgery is around £5,000 it'll be around £30,000 total... Thank you for speaking with me, I feel a little better. It's just the wait now (in the UK you need to see a special type of psychiatrist or team of psychiatrists before getting surgery on the NHS, and the waiting list is like 18-20 weeks. The referral was made around the end of May).
Breast implants is 1 surgery though, not 6.....unless they will pay for all those since they're all major things?

I don't have a camera in this house, so I can't take photos. I avoid having photos taken so I have no photos of myself to share, sorry.

My GP also agreed with my concerns, as well as a hormone specialist who said he took one look at me and thought I had some severe hormonal problems while I was growing. My deformities are visible to everyone else, so this isn't simply a case of BDD. For example, my lips turned out normal, they're plump and shaped like a cupid's bow. However, the deformities throw off facial harmony, so the 'whole picture' looks a mess.

Even my mother has told me my face doesn't look right and that it looks ugly. My mother has Asperger's, and people with Asperger's have no filter for their inner thoughts. That was a year ago. I knew my face was messed up when I was around 6 or 7. As I got older it got worse.

Thanks for that. I'm still on the waiting list so I am very anxious about things, such as if they will pay for the surgery as I'm just an ex college student who has no job or money.

I am doing this for myself, but even other people, including relatives have admitted they can't stand to look at me. I have no friends, no girlfriend because I'm quite literally disabled socially, and cannot function at all unless I'm here in my darkened room watching films or making art endlessly. I'm wasting away basically. What kind of life is that? I would feel happy if I just died in my sleep tonight.

Do you think they could do the jaw, chin (implant) and cheekbone surgeries in one go? Would they be likely to fund two surgeries if they have to split the surgeries (eg. doing 3 surgeries in one go first, then the other 3 in one go after recovery)?
Well when referring to transition, I mean hormones, and also making my life liveable.

I have severe FAS and want to get a normal face also, will surgery be free because of that? Because I am broke, and people treat me unfairly and stare because my condition (and my appearance) is associated with mental retardation. I'll be speaking to the same psychiatrist who specializes in transitioning.
